messages.content: New one to start. Twin Cities distributor wants me for a Tuesday lunch-and-learn, then Wednesday morning at a food plant south of Minneapolis for a CIP skid review. I need a first pass on flights, hotel area, and rental car. Monday afternoon departure from the Bay Area. Return date is still squishy.

Got it. What week are we talking, and is the Tuesday session at the distributor branch near MSP/Bloomington or somewhere farther out? Also, should I treat SFO as the main airport and OAK/SJC as backups?

Week of Jan 12. Tuesday Jan 13 at the Bloomington branch, lunch slot 11:30 to 1:00 with a little setup before. Wednesday Jan 14 at the plant near Lakeville, exact escort time not locked but probably early. Start with SFO, but OAK is fine if it is materially better. I care more about routing and timing than the airline on this one.
Thanks. For the return, should I build two versions: Wednesday evening if the plant releases you after the review, and Thursday morning if they add a validation readout?

Exactly. They may want a late-Wednesday validation readout, not sure yet. Also the demo sample case is supposed to arrive at the branch before I do, but I don’t have receiving confirmation. Rental car at MSP terminal, just me and the case if I end up moving it.

Flight shortlist for Mon Jan 12, planning inventory only until we verify fares: best fit is the SFO-MSP nonstop around 2:15-7:53 p.m. on Delta. It protects the afternoon departure, avoids a connection, and still gets you to the hotel with time for dinner and Tuesday prep. Acceptable backup is United SFO-DEN-MSP around 1:25-8:42 p.m.; one reasonable connection, but it arrives later and adds a failure point. OAK value backup is Southwest OAK-DEN-MSP around 12:55-8:35 p.m.; usually cheaper, but it is earlier out of the Bay Area and not as clean. I would only choose OAK if the fare gap is meaningful or SFO pricing jumps.
Good. Include a United option, but don’t rank it over the nonstop just because it’s United.
Agreed. On this route the nonstop is the cleaner schedule. United stays in the comparison as an acceptable one-stop backup, not the lead option unless fare rules or availability change.
Hotels: compare an airport-area option against Bloomington or Eagan. I don’t need downtown Minneapolis. I do want a sane Wednesday drive and not a sad dinner situation.

Hotel area comparison: Airport-area practical pick is Hyatt Place Bloomington/MSP Airport-South, usually around a 4.2 guest rating, free breakfast, easier parking than the terminal hotel, and quick access to I-494/35W. It is good for the Bloomington branch and acceptable for Lakeville, but dinner choices are more utilitarian unless you drive toward Mall of America or Bloomington restaurants. Higher-rated Eagan pick is Omni Viking Lakes, around a 4.6 guest rating, stronger room quality, on-site restaurant, and easier southbound access for the Wednesday plant visit. It will cost more but is the best fit if the plant start lands early. True airport-connected option is InterContinental MSP, around 4.4 and very easy after arrival, but parking is expensive and it is less useful once you have the rental car.
If the plant is near Lakeville, does Eagan save enough time over Bloomington to matter?

For a normal morning, Eagan is probably 25-30 minutes to the Lakeville area; Bloomington is more like 30-40 depending on where you start and traffic on 35W. Not a huge difference, but Eagan is the cleaner early-start choice and has better dinner built in. Bloomington is better only if Tuesday convenience and lower rate matter more.
Do those rooms have the basics? Coffee, mini-fridge. I don’t want to chase that later if we can avoid it.

Hyatt Place is the safer bet for both in-room coffee and a mini-fridge as standard. Omni should have in-room coffee and typically has a mini-fridge or beverage cooler setup, but I’d confirm the refrigerator language before booking if you need it for samples or perishables. InterContinental can vary by room type, so I’d treat that as ask-before-booking.
Car size? It’s one roll bag, laptop bag, and maybe the sample case if receiving is weird.

Compact is fine if the sample case is the small Pelican-style one. If it is the longer calibration kit, I’d reserve intermediate at MSP and still let you choose a compact-looking car if the trunk is decent. Pickup Monday about 8:10 p.m. at Terminal 1 works with the SFO nonstop; return can stay flexible until we choose Wednesday evening versus Thursday morning.
Split the return choices for the note. I don’t want to book the wrong one until the plant decides.

Return planning: if no validation readout, target a Wednesday nonstop MSP-SFO after about 6:30 p.m.; that means leaving the Lakeville area by roughly 3:45-4:00, allowing for fuel, rental return, and MSP security. If they add an end-of-day readout, Thursday morning is cleaner: look for an 8:00-9:00 a.m. MSP-SFO nonstop or one short connection if the nonstop is overpriced. Provisional plan to hold: Mon SFO-MSP nonstop, rental car at MSP, Omni Viking Lakes as best-fit hotel, Hyatt Place Bloomington/MSP as acceptable backup, and return ask-before-booking until the validation readout and sample-case receiving are confirmed.

messages.content: Twin Cities update. Demo case is confirmed at the branch Monday morning, and the plant locked a 7:00 a.m. escort for Wednesday. Tuesday also expanded: 9:30 calibration review before the lunch-and-learn. Need to narrow the outbound and hotel now. Return still unresolved.
Thanks. Just confirming the locations stayed the same: Tuesday at the Bloomington branch, Wednesday near Lakeville?
Yes. Bloomington branch Tuesday, Lakeville-area plant Wednesday. They may still ask for a 4:00 p.m. validation readout Wednesday.

Then I’d narrow the outbound to the SFO-MSP nonstop around 2:15-7:53 p.m. Monday. The cheaper OAK one-stop around 12:55-8:35 p.m. is workable, but it arrives later, takes a connection, and cuts into prep for the 9:30 Tuesday review. United via Denver is acceptable backup, but not better than the nonstop.
The OAK option is about $120 less. Enough to matter?

I would not take the savings for this trip. With the Tuesday agenda moved earlier and a 7:00 Wednesday escort, the nonstop is the better fit. OAK is only an acceptable backup if the SFO fare jumps or the nonstop sells out.
Hotel: airport versus Eagan. The Eagan one was Omni Viking Lakes?

Yes. Omni Viking Lakes in Eagan is the better match now: higher guest feedback, on-site restaurant, easier southbound drive to Lakeville, and still reasonable for Bloomington Tuesday. The airport-area Hyatt Place is cheaper and simpler after landing, but dinner and the Wednesday drive are weaker.
Any issue getting from Eagan to the Bloomington branch by 9:30 Tuesday?
No major issue. I’d leave the hotel around 8:35 to give yourself a 25-35 minute drive plus parking/setup buffer. If there is weather, leave closer to 8:15.
Car timing?

Pickup MSP Terminal 1 around 8:10 p.m. Monday after the nonstop lands. Reserve intermediate rather than compact so the case is not a trunk puzzle. Keep the car through Thursday morning for now; if you fly Wednesday evening, return it around 5:30-6:00 p.m. after fueling.
Send me the narrowed note. Mark the return as not ready to book yet.

Twin Cities narrowed plan: Mon Jan 12 take the SFO-MSP nonstop around 2:15-7:53 p.m.; OAK one-stop is the cost backup but not worth switching for a $120 savings. Pick up an intermediate rental at MSP Terminal 1 around 8:10 p.m. Hotel best fit is Omni Viking Lakes in Eagan for stronger guest feedback, on-site dinner, and the cleaner Wednesday Lakeville drive; airport Hyatt Place remains the acceptable backup if rate matters. Tue Jan 13 leave hotel 8:15-8:35 for the 9:30 Bloomington calibration review, then 11:30 lunch-and-learn. Wed Jan 14 leave Eagan about 5:55 a.m. for the 7:00 plant escort. Return is ask-before-booking: late Wednesday nonstop only if they release you before the 4:00 validation window; otherwise Thursday morning is the clean plan.
